_what: Which sources are FILE-SHAPED -- their acquired material is files on disk with a locator that maps to a filename -- and for those, what unread material is declared and why.
_what_it_rests_on: The claims' own `source_record` locators. NOT the source_record tables: RS-G3 is red, 27 of 481 stores declare one at all, and the largest store in the archive (739,486 claims) declares none. A check resting on that coverage would be measuring the declaration a second time.
_refuse_by_default: A source with claims that appears in NEITHER list is a failure. Silence is not an exemption -- that is the whole defect this gate exists for.
_locator_to_file: How a cited locator becomes a filename. `basename` takes the last path segment; `flatten_slashes` replaces / with _ , which is how the PFA cache is stored; `identity` is a path relative to the source directory.

wikipedia-en.unit: an article, read for one KIND of fact and not another
wikipedia-en.why_no_denominator: The failure here is not an unread article. Every predicate the store holds is person-scoped, and the archive holds no club, season, draft or standings article at all -- so 255 of the 1950 draft's 391 picks are missing from a source already held and already allowed. Nothing on disk records that a page had a draft table nobody looked at. To check it, the gate would have to know what a source COULD have yielded, and that knowledge only exists after somebody reads it.

Three separate reasons, and they are not the same reason: (1) the person sections have no cached index, so their size is unknown; (2) the link graph is a lower bound by construction and can never bound a section from above; (3) the ingest recorded no skip list, so on-disk-minus-cited cannot be attributed. not_file_shaped._enumerable_parts: A source whose WHOLE has no denominator may still have PARTS that do. Every entry here must say which -- `enumerable_parts` naming each part, its unit, how its denominator is obtained, and the three counts where they are known (exists / on disk / cited); `not_enumerable` saying what remains unmeasurable and why. `unknown` is a permitted value and is not a failure; an ABSENT list is. Evidence: Phil Flanagan, a 1936 New York Giants ninth-round pick, is not in the archive. He is on PFA's own 1936 NFL draft page, which was fetched in the original ingest and has sat unread on disk ever since. This entry said PFA had no denominator, and that was true of PFA whole and false of PFA's draft pages: they are one per year per league per kind, 203 on disk, and enumerating them took minutes and needed no network. The declaration's silence read as 'cannot be measured' when the truth was 'nobody said which half could be'.
